thread:
sam: noticing p99 streaming token spikes + a spike in reorders reported by NIC telemetry across az-b.
sam: app-side manifests as token stalls and grpc deadlines around 600-800ms, even though raw compute p95 is steady.
elaine: saw alerts from trace pipeline too, correlating with large bursts in tx_queue_suppress on several hosts :facepalm:
chris: is this the same microburst thing we fixed last quarter? different symptom?
sam: similar surface but different pattern — packets not lost, just significantly out-of-order. tcp_retrans = low.
network-lead: from NIC stats it looks like phase-shift bursts where hardware coalescing queues flush in big batches -> reordering across flows.
k8s-oncall: which pools are affected? only az-b GPU pools or cross-az?
sam: primarily az-b gpu-pool-2, a few nodes in gpu-pool-1. East-west traffic internal to the rack shows the worst numbers.
elaine: paste of tcpdump snippet from kube-node-17:

```
17:23:11.482123 IP 10.0.3.17.50050 > 10.0.3.22.55321: Flags [.], seq 12345:12467, ack 9876, win 501, length 122
17:23:11.482124 IP 10.0.3.22.55321 > 10.0.3.17.50050: Flags [.], seq 9876:10123, ack 12467, win 512, length 247
17:23:11.482220 IP 10.0.3.17.50050 > 10.0.3.22.55321: Flags [.], seq 12467:12589, ack 10123, win 501, length 122
```

sam: see the tiny interleaving; ordering flips for blocks of packets.
chris: any MTU mismatches? fragmentation would show different signs.
elaine: `ip link show` consistent MTU 9000 on both ends. no fragmentation in tcpdump.
network-lead: RDMA counters show qps reset spikes around the same time on mlx5 drivers.
k8s-oncall: did we recently push any NIC firmware/drivers or host kernel updates in az-b?
sam: we rolled a daemonset update 2 hours before the first alert — it included a new NIC offload config: GRO=on, LRO=off, tso=on. Can't be a coincidence.
chris: try toggling GRO off on one affected node to compare. quick test cmd:

```
# on node
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
```

elaine: I'm seeing the queue suppression counters drop after that on kube-node-17, latency p99 improved ~120ms in the next minute :thumbsup:
network-lead: that suggests hardware coalescing + GSO interaction producing reordered flushes. we should roll back the daemonset change and stage a controlled rollout.
sam: rolling back now to previous offload defaults on the daemonset.
ops-bot: rollback deployment red-nic-offload to v1.3 triggered by sam at 17:30 UTC
chris: also let's mark affected nodes as unschedulable and drain non-critical pods to run more tests without impacting jobs.
k8s-oncall: draining nodes gpu-pool-2-3 and gpu-pool-1-7. pods evicted.
elaine: after rollback, GRPC deadline errors dropped to baseline and reorder counters returned to normal in ~12 minutes.
network-lead: action items:
- revert NIC offload change in daemonset permanently until we validate under load (assigned: sam)
- run controlled perf experiment with different combinations (GRO/GSO/TSO) on canary nodes (assigned: chris)
- check firmware versions across az-b and schedule upgrade window if needed (assigned: network-lead)
- add telemetry alert for tx_queue_suppress > threshold and simultaneous reorder_pct > 2% (assigned: elaine)

sam: adding cost note — if we had fallen back to reserved-capacity routing to cross-az it would have added ~20% egress + 10% tail latency; avoid unless necessary.
chris: we should also consider adding an automated rollback to daemonset changes that touch NIC flags if reorder alerts fire within X minutes.
elaine: filing a short post-incident note after we confirm stable for 24h. I'll include timelines and mitigation steps.
network-lead: long-term: coordinate with vendor on driver/GRO interaction; consider kernel tuning or pinning to known-good driver until vendor patch.
sam: thanks all — monitoring for 2h, will re-open if anything flares.
ops-bot: incident-severity: low -> resolved (auto) at 17:42 UTC :white_check_mark:
